checks.q: In a sodium-cooled fast reactor, where would crystallized sodium hydride and sodium oxide collect if the sodium were not purified?
o: At the cold points of the sodium loops
At the hottest point of the core
Only in the cover gas
Only on the pump impellers
checks.x: Without purification, these impurities collect in crystallized form at the cold points of the sodium loops.

checks.q: According to the cold trap lesson plan, what are the primary origins of impurities in sodium coolant?
o: Corrosion, moisture from system component surfaces, and air intrusion
Fission of the sodium itself
Argon dissolving from the cover gas
Neutron capture in the cold trap mesh
checks.x: Impurities originate primarily from corrosion, moisture from system component surfaces, and air intrusion into the system.

body.text: The BN-600 is a sodium-cooled fast breeder reactor at the Beloyarsk Nuclear Power Station in Russia. On 21 January 1987, with the reactor at rated power, changes were noted for 7 minutes in sodium level, core reactivity and sodium pump power.
body.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.3 Safety Minute

body.text: The block of impurities disturbed core hydraulics and neutronics.
body.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.3 Safety Minute

body.text: Since then, leaks into the core cover gas have been minimized, and more advanced purification is done.
body.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.3 Safety Minute

checks.q: What caused the 1987 BN-600 transient at rated power?
o: A chunk of impurities formed from the cover gas dropped from the reactor roof
A sodium pump shaft seized
A control rod was withdrawn in error
A cold trap line froze
checks.x: The incident was attributed to a chunk of impurities, formed from impurities in the cover gas, dropping from the reactor roof.

body.text: Other impurities include metals such as iron and chromium, some of their active isotopes activated by neutron flux, carbonated particles and calcium oxide.

examples.title: Cold trap sodium running too hot or too cold
examples.page: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.12 Cold traps
examples.problem: A cold trap normally runs in the typical 230°F to 300°F range. What is the risk if its sodium runs above that range, and what is the risk if it is cooled too far below it?
steps: Too high: particulates may not effectively precipitate, so impurity removal is reduced.
Too low: the sodium may freeze and solidify.
Frozen sodium could block the system, the trap or the plugging temperature circuit, and recovery can be difficult and costly.
examples.answer: Too hot reduces impurity removal. Too cold risks freezing and blockage.
examples.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.12 Cold traps

facts.q: What are the main forms of impurity in SFR sodium coolant?
facts.a: Hydrides, oxides, metallic compounds, and metallic and carbon particles.

facts.q: Which impurities do sodium cold traps remove?
facts.a: Oxygen, hydrogen and carbon impurities, from the primary and intermediate sodium coolant loops.

facts.q: What does a cold trap economizer do?
facts.a: It acts as a regenerative heat exchanger and pre-heats the clean sodium re-entering the system.

facts.q: What sodium impurity level can a cold trap achieve?
What are the two ways to regenerate a sodium cold trap?
Why can sodium hydroxide formation be a concern in sodium systems?
facts.a: It can lead to rapid and aggressive caustic stress corrosion cracking.

facts.q: What is adsorption, as used by RVC cesium filters?
facts.a: A process by which chemical bonds form between the adsorbed material and the surface of the filter media.
A chunk of impurities, formed from impurities in the cover gas, dropped from the reactor roof and disturbed core hydraulics and neutronics.

summary.text: Impurities form in sodium from corrosion, moisture and air intrusion, and would collect as crystals at cold points.
summary.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.2 Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification

summary.text: Cold traps are the main sodium purification devices. They cool a small fraction of the flow to just above the sodium freezing point so impurities precipitate on the mesh.
summary.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.10 Cold Trap

summary.text: Typical cold trap temperature is 230°F to 300°F. Too hot reduces removal, and too cold risks freezing.
summary.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.12 Cold traps

summary.text: As impurities build up, the temperature at which crystallization occurs rises. A plugging temperature indicator uses this.
summary.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.15 Plugging Temperature Indicator

summary.text: Temperature and flow are controlled to avoid liquid oxygen, sodium oxide plugging and sodium freezing.
summary.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.20 Cautions

summary.text: A loaded cold trap is regenerated ex-situ or in-situ.
summary.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.21 Regeneration

summary.text: RVC filters remove cesium by chemical adsorption, which is slow and irreversible, so spent traps need long-term disposal.
summary.cite: Word: Cold Traps and Sodium Coolant Purification.docx, slide 1.31 Long-Term immobilization and Storage
